stories.headline: Trump Admin Considers EO to Vet AI Models Before Release, Reversing Hands-Off Stance

key_facts.fact: The White House is discussing an executive order to create a working group of tech executives and government officials to examine potential review procedures for new AI models before public release
key_facts.excerpt: The White House is discussing an executive order that would establish a working group of tech executives and government officials to examine potential review procedures for new AI models

key_facts.fact: Senior administration officials briefed executives from Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI on some of the plans in meetings last week
key_facts.excerpt: Senior administration officials briefed executives from Anthropic, Google and OpenAI on some of the plans in meetings last week

key_facts.fact: The immediate catalyst was Anthropic's Mythos model, whose cybersecurity vulnerability-finding capabilities prompted national security concerns
key_facts.excerpt: The immediate catalyst was the emergence of a powerful new AI model called Mythos, built by the San Francisco start-up Anthropic. The company has described the model's ability to identify software security vulnerabilities as potentially leading to a cybersecurity reckoning

key_facts.fact: The shift follows David Sacks' departure as White House AI czar in March; Susie Wiles and Scott Bessent have taken over AI policy
key_facts.excerpt: Silicon Valley insider David Sacks, the former White House AI czar who championed deregulation, departed from the role in March. White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent have stepped in

key_facts.fact: Critics say this amounts to a de facto licensing regime; ITIF president Daniel Castro called it a 'full embrace of the precautionary principle'
key_facts.excerpt: Daniel Castro, the president of science and tech think tank ITIF, listed several reasons the potential executive order is a 'terrible idea' on X. First, he said it is a 'full embrace' of the precautionary principle

sources.title: White House Weighs Vetting AI Models Before Public Release: Report

stories.headline: Sierra Raises $950M Series E at $15.8B Valuation, Serves 40% of Fortune 50 With AI Agents

key_facts.fact: Sierra raised $950 million in a Series E led by Tiger Global and GV (Google Ventures), at a $15.8 billion post-money valuation, up from $10 billion in 2025
key_facts.excerpt: The San Francisco-based company brought in $950 million in fresh capital at a $15.8 post-money valuation, led by Tiger and Google's GV. Benchmark, Sequoia, Greenoaks and other existing investors also participated.

key_facts.fact: Sierra now serves over 40% of the Fortune 50 and surpassed $150 million in annual recurring revenue in just eight quarters
key_facts.excerpt: Now, Sierra is serving over 40% of the Fortune 50, and agents built on our platform are powering billions of customer interactions

key_facts.fact: CEO Bret Taylor estimates $400 billion is spent annually on customer service, with most of that shifting to AI agents
key_facts.excerpt: Taylor estimated that $400 billion is spent annually on customer service, with most of that shifting to AI agents

key_facts.fact: Sierra uses a 'constellation of models' from OpenAI and Anthropic alongside its own fine-tuned proprietary layers
key_facts.excerpt: Taylor told CNBC the company employs a 'constellation of models' as well its own fine-tuned proprietary layers

key_facts.fact: Customers include Prudential, Cigna, Blue Cross Blue Shield, Rocket Mortgage, and one in three of the world's largest banks
key_facts.excerpt: Sierra's customers are mostly enterprises like Prudential, Cigna, Blue Cross Blue Shield and Rocket Mortgage, as well as one in three of the world's largest banks

key_facts.fact: Sierra launched Ghostwriter in April, an 'agent as a service' tool that autonomously creates and deploys specialized agents from natural language descriptions
key_facts.excerpt: In April, the company launched Ghostwriter, an 'agent as a service' tool designed to build other agents. Users describe what they need in natural language, and Ghostwriter autonomously creates and deploys a specialized agent

stories.headline: Palantir Reports 85% Revenue Growth to $1.63B in Q1, Raises FY26 Guidance to 71% Growth

key_facts.fact: Palantir reported Q1 revenue of $1.63 billion, up 85% YoY (its fastest growth since going public in 2020), beating estimates of $1.54 billion
key_facts.excerpt: Palantir's revenue grew about 85% in the quarter, according to a statement, marking the fastest increase in sales since at least 2020, the year the company went public through a direct listing.

key_facts.fact: US commercial revenue surged 133% YoY to $595 million; US government revenue grew 84% YoY to $687 million
key_facts.excerpt: U.S. commercial revenue grew 133% year-over-year and 18% quarter-over-quarter to $595 million. U.S. government revenue grew 84% year-over-year and 21% quarter-over-quarter to $687 million

key_facts.fact: Palantir raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $7.65-$7.66 billion (71% YoY growth), up from prior guidance of $7.18-$7.20 billion, above $7.27B consensus
key_facts.excerpt: The company sees $7.65 billion to $7.66 billion in 2026 revenue, an annual jump of 71% and higher than the $7.27 billion LSEG consensus

key_facts.fact: CEO Alex Karp said Palantir's Rule of 40 score reached 145%, and predicts the US business will double again in 2027
key_facts.excerpt: Palantir's Rule of 40 score has soared to 145%. We have shattered the metric, a feat matched only by other fellow AI infrastructure companies: NVIDIA, Micron and SK hynix

key_facts.fact: Adjusted EPS was $0.33 vs $0.28 expected; GAAP net income quadrupled YoY to $870.5 million (53% margin)
key_facts.excerpt: Net income roughly quadrupled to $870.5 million, or 34 cents per share, from $214 million, or 8 cents per share, a year earlier

key_facts.fact: Palantir closed 206 deals worth over $1 million, 47 deals exceeding $10 million, with total contract value of $2.41 billion (up 61% YoY)
key_facts.excerpt: Closed 206 deals of at least $1 million, 72 deals of at least $5 million, and 47 deals of at least $10 million. Closed total contract value of $2.41 billion, up 61% year-over-year

sources.title: Palantir (PLTR) Q1 earnings report 2026

stories.headline: SAP Acquires Prior Labs With €1B Commitment to Build Europe's Leading Frontier AI Lab for Tabular Data

key_facts.fact: SAP entered a definitive agreement to acquire Prior Labs, committing to invest more than €1 billion over four years to scale it into a globally leading frontier AI lab for structured business data
key_facts.excerpt: SAP committing to invest more than €1 billion over the next four years to scale it into a globally leading frontier AI lab for the structured data that runs the world's businesses

key_facts.fact: Prior Labs built TabPFN, a tabular foundation model with over 3 million downloads, purpose-built for structured data predictions where LLMs struggle
key_facts.excerpt: With over 3 million downloads, Prior Labs' TabPFN is a widely adopted open-source tool for tabular AI, supporting a dynamic developer ecosystem

key_facts.fact: SAP also announced the acquisition of Dremio, a data lakehouse platform with $300M+ in prior funding, to enhance its Business Data Cloud offering
key_facts.excerpt: Santa Clara, California-based Dremio Inc. raised more than $300 million prior to the deal... Dremio has built a data management platform that can store and analyze large volumes of business information

key_facts.fact: Prior Labs will continue operating independently, retaining its Freiburg, Berlin, and New York locations, and maintaining its open-source strategy
key_facts.excerpt: Despite the acquisition, Prior Labs will remain an independent unit, including its brand, research approach, open source strategy and existing customer relationships

key_facts.fact: Prior Labs' cofounders Frank Hutter, Noah Hollmann, and Sauraj Gambhir work with leading scientists including Yann LeCun
key_facts.excerpt: The Prior Labs cofounders Frank Hutter, Noah Hollmann and Sauraj Gambhir lead a team of world-class AI researchers and practitioners. The company works with leading scientists in the field, including Yann LeCun

sources.title: SAP to Acquire Prior Labs to Establish a Globally Leading Frontier AI Lab in Europe

stories.headline: DeepInfra Raises $107M Series B Backed by Nvidia to Scale Open-Model Inference Cloud

key_facts.fact: DeepInfra raised $107 million in a Series B co-led by 500 Global and Georges Harik (one of Google's first cloud engineers), with participation from Nvidia, Samsung Next, and Supermicro
key_facts.excerpt: The round is co-led by 500 Global and Georges Harik, with participation from A.Capital Ventures, Crescent Cove, Felicis, NVIDIA, Peak6, Samsung Next, Supermicro, and Upper90

key_facts.fact: DeepInfra grew its token processing volume by 25x since its Series A, operating its own GPU infrastructure across eight US data centers
key_facts.excerpt: Since our Series A, we've grown the volume of tokens we process by 25x

key_facts.fact: The platform currently supports 190+ open-weight models and uses Nvidia's Dynamo distributed-inference platform and Vera Rubin GPUs for 20x greater inference cost efficiency
key_facts.excerpt: The startup operates its own hardware across eight data centers in the U.S. and uses Nvidia's Dynamo distributed-inference platform and Vera Rubin GPUs for 20-times greater inference cost efficiency

key_facts.fact: DeepInfra argues inference, not training, is now the dominant AI workload constraint, with a single agentic task requiring 50 to 100+ model calls
key_facts.excerpt: agent-based systems are driving continuous, high-volume token demand — a single agentic task can require 50 to 100+ model calls and run nonstop

key_facts.fact: The company was founded by the same team that built imo, a messaging app used by 200M+ people, bringing expertise in high-throughput distributed systems
key_facts.excerpt: the team behind DeepInfra also built imo, the messenger app used by 200M+ people worldwide

stories.headline: Cisco Acquires Astrix Security for ~$400M to Secure AI Agents and Non-Human Identities

key_facts.fact: Cisco announced the acquisition of Israeli startup Astrix Security for approximately $400 million to bolster its AI agent security portfolio
key_facts.excerpt: Cisco announced on Monday the completion of its acquisition of Israeli cybersecurity company Astrix Security. Calcalist has learned that the final purchase price is approximately $400 million.

key_facts.fact: Astrix specializes in securing non-human identities (NHIs) — API keys, service accounts, OAuth tokens, and the credentials AI agents use to access systems at scale
key_facts.excerpt: Astrix Security has focused on securing the identities and credentials that power modern systems — API keys, service accounts, and OAuth tokens — the very credentials that AI Agents are now using (and abusing) to gain access and execute work at scale

key_facts.fact: According to Cisco's AI Readiness Index, only 24% of organizations can control AI agent actions with proper guardrails and live monitoring
key_facts.excerpt: According to Cisco's AI Readiness Index, only 24% of organizations can control agent actions with proper guardrails and live monitoring, and just 31% feel fully capable of securing their agent AI systems

key_facts.fact: Astrix was founded in 2021 by Alon Jackson and Idan Gour, veterans of Israel's Unit 8200, and raised $85 million in total prior to the deal
key_facts.excerpt: Founded in 2021 by Alon Jackson and Idan Gour, both veterans of Israel's elite Unit 8200, Astrix has positioned itself around what it describes as a critical blind spot in modern cybersecurity

key_facts.fact: Cisco will integrate Astrix into Cisco Identity Intelligence, Secure Access, and Duo IAM, with data feeding into Splunk for unified agent activity monitoring
key_facts.excerpt: Cisco plans to integrate Astrix Security's capabilities into Cisco Identity Intelligence, strengthening visibility and context across identities within the Cisco Security platform, as well as to extend these capabilities into Cisco's zero trust access portfolio

sources.title: Cisco acquires AI security startup Astrix for $400 million

stories.headline: Kuo: OpenAI Fast-Tracking AI Agent Phone With Custom MediaTek Chip, Mass Production H1 2027

key_facts.fact: Analyst Ming-Chi Kuo reports OpenAI is fast-tracking its first AI agent phone, with mass production targeted as early as H1 2027, accelerated from prior 2028 timeline
key_facts.excerpt: According to Kuo, OpenAI may accelerate development of its first smartphone, targeting mass production as early as the first half of 2027

key_facts.fact: MediaTek is currently the leading candidate as sole processor supplier, with a customized Dimensity 9600 chip built on TSMC's N2P (2nm) process node in H2 2026
key_facts.excerpt: MediaTek is currently the leading candidate to supply the processor, which is expected to be a customised chip based on the MediaTek Dimensity 9600 and manufactured using TSMC's N2P process in the second half of 2026

key_facts.fact: The device features a dual NPU architecture for layered AI computing, LPDDR6 RAM, and UFS 5.0 storage to handle continuous on-device AI workloads
key_facts.excerpt: The hardware is said to focus heavily on AI-driven tasks, with a dual NPU architecture designed for layered computing. Memory and storage could also see upgrades with LPDDR6 RAM and UFS 5.0

key_facts.fact: The phone is designed around AI agents rather than apps — users express intent and agents handle tasks directly, replacing the traditional app-based interaction model
key_facts.excerpt: Instead of relying on multiple apps, the focus could shift to AI agents that handle tasks directly based on user intent

key_facts.fact: Potential drivers include supporting OpenAI's year-end IPO narrative and intensifying competition in AI agent phones; shipments could reach 30 million units across 2027-2028
key_facts.excerpt: Potential drivers include supporting a year-end IPO narrative and intensifying competition in AI agent phones

sources.title: OpenAI agent phone to be powered by 2nm Dimensity 9600
OpenAI AI phone may arrive as soon as next year with MediaTek chip, says Kuo
